'''Temasek Holdings (Private) Limited''' ({{IPAc-en|ipa|t|ə|ˈ|m|ɑː|s|eɪ|k}} {{respell|tə|MAH|sayk}}{{NoteTag|Alternatively, {{IPAc-en|t|ə|ˈ|m|ɑː|s|ɪ|k}} {{respell|tə|MAH|sikk}}.}}) is a Singaporean [[State ownership|state-owned]] multinational investment firm. Incorporated on 25 June 1974, Temasek has a net portfolio of S$518 billion as of 31 March 2026.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Temasek’s Net Portfolio Value Grows to S$518 billion, up S$49 billion from Last Year|url=https://www.temasek.com.sg/en/news-and-resources/news-room/news/2026/temasek-net-portfolio-value-grows-to-518b-up-49b-from-last-year |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250812164834/https://www.temasek.com.sg/en/news-and-resources/news-room/news/2026/temasek-net-portfolio-value-grows-to-518b-up-49b-from-last-year |archive-date=2025-08-12 |access-date=2026-07-10 |website=Temasek Corporate Website |language=en}}</ref> Headquartered at [[Orchard Road]], Singapore, it has 13 offices in nine countries around the world, including in [[Beijing]], [[Brussels]], [[Hanoi]], [[London]], [[Mexico City]], [[Mumbai]], [[New York City]], [[Paris]], [[San Francisco]], [[Shanghai]], [[Shenzhen]], and [[Washington D.C.]]<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 July 2021|title=Temasek Review 2026|url=https://www.temasekreview.com.sg/downloads/Temasek-Review-2026-full-version.pdf|website=Temasek Review Website|access-date=10 July 2026|archive-date=21 September 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210921223100/https://www.temasek.com.sg/en/news-and-views/news-room/news/2021/temasek-review-2021-bounce-forward|url-status=live}}</ref>

It is an active shareholder and investor, with four key structural trends guiding its long term portfolio construction—Digitisation, Sustainable Living, Future of Consumption, and Longer Lifespans.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Chan |first=Genevieve |date=5 December 2021 |title=Four keys that could unlock a better, more sustainable world |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/invest/four-keys-that-could-unlock-a-better-more-sustainable-world |access-date= |website=The Straits Times |archive-date=12 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220812040600/https://www.straitstimes.com/business/invest/four-keys-that-could-unlock-a-better-more-sustainable-world |url-status=live }}</ref> Temasek's portfolio covers a broad spectrum of sectors. Its key focus investment areas include Consumer, Media & Technology, Life Sciences & Agri-Food, and Non-Bank Financial Services.<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 July 2021|title=Temasek Review 2021|url=https://www.temasekreview.com.sg/downloads/Temasek-Review-2021-Presentation-Slides.pdf#page=9|website=Temasek Review|access-date=January 9, 2026|archive-date=18 April 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220418213854/https://www.temasekreview.com.sg/downloads/Temasek-Review-2021-Presentation-Slides.pdf#page=9|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Temasek has held overall corporate global [[credit ratings]] of "Aaa/AAA" by rating agencies [[Moody's]]<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.temasek.com.sg/en/about-us/temasek-at-a-glance |title=Temasek at a Glance |author= <!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date= 31 March 2025  |publisher= Temasek Holdings (Private) Limited |access-date= 26 April 2026 |url-status=live
|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20260426021347/https://www.temasek.com.sg/en/about-us/temasek-at-a-glance |archive-date= 26 April 2026 }}</ref> and [[Standard & Poor's]]<ref>{{Cite news |date=9 August 2021 |title=S&P Global Ratings |url=https://www.temasek.com.sg/en/our-financials/library/credit-rating-reports |access-date=12 August 2022 |archive-date=14 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220814212456/https://www.temasek.com.sg/en/our-financials/library/credit-rating-reports |url-status=live }}</ref> respectively since its inaugural credit ratings in 2004. It has also attained perfect quarterly scores<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.asiaone.com/News/The+Business+Times/Story/A1Story20090605-146491.html|title=Temasek hits perfect score on transparency index|date=5 June 2009|work=AsiaOne|access-date=2 December 2019|archive-date=20 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191220093221/https://www.asiaone.com/News/The+Business+Times/Story/A1Story20090605-146491.html|url-status=live}}</ref> on the Linaburg-Maduell Transparency Index, a measure of the openness of government-owned investment funds. Temasek is primarily anchored in Asia, with underlying country exposure of 27% Singapore, 26% China, 17% Americas, 12% Asia Pacific (excluding Singapore, China and India), 11% Europe, Middle East and Africa, and 7% India as at 31 March 2026. <ref>{{Cite web|title=Temasek Review 2026|url=https://www.temasekreview.com.sg/downloads/Temasek-Review-2026-full-version.pdf|website=Temasek Review Website|language=en|access-date=10 July 2026|archive-date=27 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211127135412/https://www.temasek.com.sg/en/what-we-do/our-portfolio|url-status=live}}</ref>

While Temasek is largely considered as being a [[sovereign wealth fund]] (SWF), there are major differences as it invests mostly in equities, is the outright owner of many assets and companies, and pays taxes like other commercial investment firms.<ref>{{cite web | url = http://www.vcpost.com/articles/19295/20131205/chairman-lim-boon-heng-temasek-unique-sovereign-wealth-fund.htm | title = Temasek is different from other sovereign wealth funds and pays tax - Chairman | website = Venture Capital Post | date = 5 December 2013 |author-first1=Nicel Jane|author-last1=Avellana| access-date = 6 April 2015 | archive-date = 9 July 2018 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180709185529/https://www.vcpost.com/articles/19295/20131205/chairman-lim-boon-heng-temasek-unique-sovereign-wealth-fund.htm | url-status = live }}</ref> 
Temasek's one-year [[total shareholder return]] (TSR) was 10.5%, with longer term 10-year and 20-year TSRs at 7.1% and 6.8% respectively, compounded annually.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |author=Temasek |first=Holdings |date=10 July 2026 |title=Temasek Review 2026 |url=https://www.temasekreview.com.sg/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180703032118/http://www.temasekreview.com.sg/? |archive-date=3 July 2018 |access-date=10 July 2018 |website=Temasek Review 2026}}</ref> In addition to Temasek, the Government of Singapore also owns [[GIC (Singaporean sovereign wealth fund)|GIC Private Limited]], a traditional SWF which manages about US$936 billion of assets as of 2026<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-02-07 |title=Singapore's $744 Billion Fund Eyes Deals in Low-Return World |language=en |work=Bloomberg.com |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-02-07/singapore-s-744-billion-fund-ramps-up-deals-in-low-return-world |access-date=2022-12-09 |archive-date=28 November 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221128231333/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-02-07/singapore-s-744-billion-fund-ramps-up-deals-in-low-return-world |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Ramli |first1=David |last2=Chanjaroen |first2=Chanyaporn |title=Singapore's GIC Set to Manage Extra $137 Billion in Reserves |url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-01-12/singapore-s-gic-set-to-manage-extra-137-billion-in-reserves |website=www.bloomberg.com |access-date=22 January 2022 |date=12 January 2022 |archive-date=11 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220311061618/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2022-01-12/singapore-s-gic-set-to-manage-extra-137-billion-in-reserves |url-status=live }}</ref> and the compulsory pension programme [[Central Provident Fund]] (CPF) with assets of US$513 billion,<ref>{{Cite web |title=CPFB {{!}} CPF statistics |url=https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/infohub/reports-and-statistics/cpf-statistics |access-date=2022-12-09 |website=www.cpf.gov.sg |language=en |archive-date=9 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221209115009/https://www.cpf.gov.sg/member/infohub/reports-and-statistics/cpf-statistics |url-status=live }}</ref> giving a total publicly known AUM of approximately US$1.97 trillion.

==Status==
Temasek is a company incorporated under the Singapore Companies Act. It is wholly owned by a government officer--the Singapore Minister for Finance, who is its single shareholder. Despite this, it claims to be neither a government agency nor a [[Statutory boards of the Singapore Government|statutory board]]. Like other commercial companies, Temasek: pays [[tax]]es in the countries in which it operates, distributes dividends (although only to a single, government shareholder), has a board of directors and a professional management team.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Corporate Governance |url=https://www.temasek.com.sg/content/temasek-corporate/en/about-us/corporate-governance |access-date=2024-07-11 |website=Temasek Corporate Website English |language=en}}</ref>

Temasek is designated a Fifth Schedule<ref name=":2" /> entity under the [[Constitution of Singapore]], which imposes certain safeguards to protect the government's [[Reserves of the Government of Singapore|past reserves]]. For instance, the approval of the [[President of Singapore]] is required for any transaction which is likely to result in a draw-down of Temasek's cash reserves.<ref>{{Cite news|date=29 September 2016|title=Shareholders approve Temasek buyout of Singapore rail operator|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-smrt-corp-m-a-temasek-holdings-idUSKCN11Z1L9|access-date=21 July 2017|archive-date=25 May 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230525014353/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-smrt-corp-m-a-temasek-holdings-idUSKCN11Z1L9|url-status=live}}</ref> The president also has the right to appoint, terminate, or renew the members of Temasek's board of directors. In most other respects, however, Temasek operates as an independent commercial investment holding company.<ref>{{cite news|title=Portfolio Performance.|url=https://www.temasek.com.sg/en/our-financials/portfolio-performance.html|access-date=17 November 2020|archive-date=12 September 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190912145205/https://www.temasek.com.sg/en/our-financials/portfolio-performance.html|url-status=live}}Retrieved 21 March 2018.</ref>

In a 2009 speech,<ref name=":0" /> [[Ho Ching]], then Temasek Holdings' Executive Director and CEO, said that the company had made an effort to instill discipline and professionalism, and to be tested and measured by providing public markers of performance. She noted that Temasek's bonds spreads and credit ratings have been regularly<ref>{{Cite web|date=18 April 2013|title=Moody's affirms Temasek's Aaa rating|url=https://www.moodys.com/research/Moodys-affirms-Temaseks-Aaa-rating--PR_271122|website=Moody's|access-date=31 October 2013|archive-date=1 October 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221001223357/https://www.moodys.com/research/Moodys-affirms-Temaseks-Aaa-rating--PR_271122|url-status=live}}</ref> and independently<ref>{{Cite news|date=15 July 2013|title=S&P CONFIRMS AAA RATING AS TEMASEK UPSIZES GLOBAL NOTES TO US$15 BILLION|url=http://asiatoday.com.au/content/sp-confirms-aaa-rating-temasek-upsizes-global-notes-us15-billion|access-date=31 October 2013|archive-date=4 November 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131104100156/http://asiatoday.com.au/content/sp-confirms-aaa-rating-temasek-upsizes-global-notes-us15-billion|url-status=live}}</ref> monitored as public markers of Temasek's financial position and credit risks. Temasek had also openly<ref>{{Cite news|date=17 July 2012|title=Tougher challenges for Temasek ahead|url=http://www.timesbusinessdirectory.com/Singlenews.aspx?DirID=86&rec_code=821045&title=Tougher%20challenges%20for%20Temasek%20ahead|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131102070607/http://www.timesbusinessdirectory.com/Singlenews.aspx?DirID=86&rec_code=821045&title=Tougher%20challenges%20for%20Temasek%20ahead|archive-date=2 November 2013|df=dmy-all}}</ref> and accurately<ref>{{Cite news|date=23 August 2011|title=Temasek Holdings responds to NSP's claims|url=https://sg.news.yahoo.com/blogs/singaporescene/nsp-next-president-champion-transparency-gic-temasek-173953147.html?nf=1|access-date=12 April 2016|archive-date=29 September 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220929091921/https://sg.news.yahoo.com/blogs/singaporescene/nsp-next-president-champion-transparency-gic-temasek-173953147.html?nf=1|url-status=live}}</ref> disclosed its financial information through its annual report (although Ho said that, as a private company, it was not legally obliged to do so).

==History==
At the point of [[History of the Republic of Singapore#Independence from Malaysia|Singapore's independence]] in August 1965, the [[Government of Singapore]] had ownership or joint ownership of various local companies, such as [[Malaysia-Singapore Airlines]] (later split up into [[Malaysia Airlines]] and [[Singapore Airlines]]) and the Singapore Telephone Board (which became [[Singapore Telecommunications]] and subsequently [[Singtel]]). As part of its push for local and foreign private investment in sectors such as manufacturing and shipbuilding, the government's [[Economic Development Board]] (EDB) also bought minority stakes in a variety of local companies.<ref>{{Cite web|title=About Singapore - Our History - The Sixties|url=http://www.edb.gov.sg/content/edb/en/why-singapore/about-singapore/our-history/1960s.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121006094315/http://www.edb.gov.sg/content/edb/en/why-singapore/about-singapore/our-history/1960s.html|archive-date=6 October 2012}}</ref> During the first ten years after independence, the government acquired or established several companies, such as the [[Keppel Corporation]] (originally Keppel Shipyard, taken over from the [[Royal Navy]] after the British military withdrawal from Singapore), [[ST Engineering]] (originally a weapon manufacturer set up to supply the [[Singapore Armed Forces]]), and the shipping company [[Neptune Orient Lines]].<ref>{{Cite news |last=Francis |first=Rozario |date=23 February 1968 |title=A takeover of 15,000 acres |work=The Straits Times |url=https://eresources.nlb.gov.sg/newspapers/Digitised/Article/straitstimes19680223-1.2.27 |access-date=12 August 2022 |archive-date=12 August 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220812040600/https://eresources.nlb.gov.sg/newspapers/Digitised/Article/straitstimes19680223-1.2.27 |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 25 June 1974, Temasek was incorporated under the Singapore Companies Act<ref name="temasek-incorporated" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Singapore Statutes Online - 50 - Companies Act|url=http://statutes.agc.gov.sg/aol/search/display/view.w3p;page=0;query=DocId%3Ac3063e4b-61ed-4faf-8014-fabd5b998ed7%20%20Status%3Ainforce%20Depth%3A0;rec=0|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121231145749/http://statutes.agc.gov.sg/aol/search/display/view.w3p;page=0;query=DocId%3Ac3063e4b-61ed-4faf-8014-fabd5b998ed7%20%20Status%3Ainforce%20Depth%3A0;rec=0|archive-date=31 December 2012}}</ref> to hold and manage the assets previously held directly by the Singapore government, named for an [[Temasek|early settlement on the island]]. The goal was for Temasek to own and manage these investments on a commercial basis,<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|date=29 July 2009|title=Speeches by Ho Ching, Executive Director & CEO, at the Institute of Policy Studies|url=http://www.temasek.com.sg/mediacentre/speeches?detailid=8600|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131102150707/http://www.temasek.com.sg/mediacentre/speeches?detailid=8600|archive-date=2 November 2013}}</ref> allowing the [[Ministry of Finance (Singapore)|Ministry of Finance]] and the [[Ministry of Trade and Industry (Singapore)|Ministry of Trade and Industry]] to focus on policymaking.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Temasek Holdings FAQs - (15 Sep 2011) {{!}} PDF {{!}} Corporations {{!}} Companies |url=https://www.scribd.com/document/76979991/Temasek-Holdings-FAQs-15-Sep-2011 |access-date=2023-07-24 |website=Scribd |language=en |archive-date=24 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724064531/https://www.scribd.com/document/76979991/Temasek-Holdings-FAQs-15-Sep-2011 |url-status=live }}</ref>

In February 2020, Temasek announced a company-wide wage freeze and voluntary pay cuts for senior management in part to help fund community programs aimed at alleviating the impact of [[Coronavirus disease 2019|COVID-19]].<ref>{{Cite news|date=23 March 2020|title=Temasek Biggest Shareholdings Fall $23.5 Billion in Three Months|newspaper=Bloomberg.com|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-03-23/temasek-biggest-shareholdings-fall-23-5-billion-in-three-months|access-date=9 September 2020|archive-date=5 December 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221205105736/https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2020-03-23/temasek-biggest-shareholdings-fall-23-5-billion-in-three-months|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 1 October 2021, [[Dilhan Pillay Sandrasegara]], the current chief executive officer of Temasek International (TI), succeeded [[Ho Ching]] as executive director and chief executive officer of Temasek Holdings.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Poon|first=Chian Hui|date=9 Feb 2021|title=Ho Ching to retire as Temasek CEO on Oct 1; Dilhan Pillay named successor|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/economy/ho-ching-to-retire-astemasek-ceo-on-oct-1-dilhan-pillay-named-successor|website=The Straits Times|access-date=16 July 2021|archive-date=27 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221127080714/http://www.straitstimes.com/business/economy/ho-ching-to-retire-astemasek-ceo-on-oct-1-dilhan-pillay-named-successor|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 6 June 2025, Temasek announced that Senior Minister and former Deputy Prime Minister Teo Chee Hean would succeed Lim Boon Heng as chairman on 9 October 2025, after joining as deputy chairman on 1 July 2025.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Ngui |first=Yantoultra |last2= |first2= |date=2025-06-06 |title=Singapore's Temasek appoints former deputy PM Teo Chee Hean as next chairman |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/asia/singapores-temasek-appoints-former-deputy-pm-teo-chee-hean-next-chairman-2025-06-06/ |access-date=2025-09-26 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref>

On 28 August 2025, Temasek announced it would create three wholly owned entities effective 1 April 2026: Temasek Global Investments, Temasek Singapore, and Temasek Partnership Solutions. Temasek International would house the firm's group and corporate functions, providing enterprise-wide governance, strategic, and operational support to these entities. As part of the changes, Chia Song Hwee became CEO of Temasek Global Investments. Other appointments include Nagi Hamiyeh, Head of Europe, Middle East and Africa, to be concurrently appointed as Temasek Global Investments' President, and Png Chin Yee, CFO, concurrently appointed as Temasek Singapore's President. <ref>{{Cite news |last=Ngui |first=Yantoultra |last2=Ngui |first2=Yantoultra |date=2025-08-28 |title=Singapore's Temasek to revamp structure to sharpen investment focus, CEO says |url=https://www.reuters.com/markets/europe/singapores-temasek-revamp-structure-sharpen-investment-focus-ceo-says-2025-08-28/ |access-date=2025-09-26 |work=Reuters |language=en}}</ref>

==Investments==
Temasek's initial portfolio of S$354 million comprised shares previously held by the Singapore Government, including a [[Jurong Bird Park|bird park]], a hotel, a shoemaker, a detergent producer, naval yards converted into a ship repair business, a start-up airline, and an iron and steel mill.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chart of the Day: Temasek's major stock investments yielded 8.1%|url=https://sbr.com.sg/markets-investing/news/chart-day-temaseks-major-stock-investments-yielded-81|website=Singapore Business Review|date=8 March 2018|access-date=9 September 2020|archive-date=17 November 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221117164437/https://sbr.com.sg/markets-investing/news/chart-day-temaseks-major-stock-investments-yielded-81|url-status=live|author-first1=Danielle|author-last1=Isaac}}</ref>

===2000s===
Temasek's [[Sale of Shin Corporation to Temasek Holdings|2006 acquisition]] of [[Shin Corporation]], owned by the family of then Thai prime minister [[Thaksin Shinawatra]], was particularly controversial, with protestors burning effigies of Lee and Ho on the streets of Bangkok.<ref name="asiamedia">{{cite web|url=http://www.international.ucla.edu/cnes/article/41204|title=Thailand: Protesters burn images of Lee, wife|work=Bangkok Post|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230218112438/https://www.international.ucla.edu/cnes/article/41204|archive-date=18 February 2023|date=18 March 2006|via=UCLA Center for Near Eastern Studies}}</ref> The deal was a factor in exacerbating the [[Thailand political crisis 2005-2006|Thai political crisis]], which eventually led to the downfall of Thaksin and a review of the transaction's legality. The [[CDRM|military junta]] that overthrew Thaksin later tried unsuccessfully to force Temasek to divest a large part of its investment in Shin Corp.<ref>[http://www.asiasentinel.com/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=337&Itemid=32 Thailand Moves Against Foreign Firms] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070927211521/http://www.asiasentinel.com/index.php?option=com_content&task=view&id=337&Itemid=32 |date=27 September 2007 }}, Asia Sentinel, 10 January 2007</ref> As of 2015, Temasek's stake in [[Intouch Holdings|Intouch Corporation]] (as Shin Corporation was renamed) had reduced to 42%.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.temasekreview.com.sg/major-investments/telecommunications-media-and-technology.html#table|title=Temasek Review|date=4 July 2015|publisher=Temasek|access-date=21 October 2015|archive-date=21 June 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190621071151/https://www.temasekreview.com.sg/major-investments/telecommunications-media-and-technology.html#table|url-status=live}}</ref> In 2016, Temasek sold a further 21% stake in Intouch Holdings, the Thai telecoms conglomerate formerly known as Shin Corp.<ref>{{Cite news|last=Lee|first=Marissa|date=2016-08-19|title=Temasek sells telco shares to Singtel for $2.47b|language=en|work=The Straits Times|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/temasek-sells-telco-shares-to-singtel-for-247b|access-date=2018-07-10|archive-date=18 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230218112451/https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/temasek-sells-telco-shares-to-singtel-for-247b|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Sustainability ==
In 2024, the company launched its inaugural sustainability report, stating that portfolio emissions were cut by 22 per cent for the financial year. Their sustainability-aligned investments accounted for 12 per cent of their net portfolio value and stood at $44 billion.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Tan |first=Sue-Ann |date=2024-07-09 |title=Temasek's portfolio emissions drop 22%; company to step up sustainable investments |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/business/companies-markets/temasek-portfolio-emissions-drop-22-per-cent-over-2023-to-increase-sustainable-living-investments |access-date=2024-07-11 |work=[[The Straits Times]] |language=en |issn=0585-3923}}</ref>

Temasek Holdings (Private) Limited (IPA:  tə-MAH-sayk) is a Singaporean state-owned multinational investment firm. Incorporated on 25 June 1974, Temasek has a net portfolio of S$518 billion as of 31 March 2026. Headquartered at Orchard Road, Singapore, it has 13 offices in nine countries around the world, including in Beijing, Brussels, Hanoi, London, Mexico City, Mumbai, New York City, Paris, San Francisco, Shanghai, Shenzhen, and Washington D.C.
It is an active shareholder and investor, with four key structural trends guiding its long term portfolio construction—Digitisation, Sustainable Living, Future of Consumption, and Longer Lifespans. Temasek's portfolio covers a broad spectrum of sectors. Its key focus investment areas include Consumer, Media & Technology, Life Sciences & Agri-Food, and Non-Bank Financial Services.
Temasek has held overall corporate global credit ratings of "Aaa/AAA" by rating agencies Moody's and Standard & Poor's respectively since its inaugural credit ratings in 2004. It has also attained perfect quarterly scores on the Linaburg-Maduell Transparency Index, a measure of the openness of government-owned investment funds. Temasek is primarily anchored in Asia, with underlying country exposure of 27% Singapore, 26% China, 17% Americas, 12% Asia Pacific (excluding Singapore, China and India), 11% Europe, Middle East and Africa, and 7% India as at 31 March 2026. 
While Temasek is largely considered as being a sovereign wealth fund (SWF), there are major differences as it invests mostly in equities, is the outright owner of many assets and companies, and pays taxes like other commercial investment firms. 
Temasek's one-year total shareholder return (TSR) was 10.5%, with longer term 10-year and 20-year TSRs at 7.1% and 6.8% respectively, compounded annually. In addition to Temasek, the Government of Singapore also owns GIC Private Limited, a traditional SWF which manages about US$936 billion of assets as of 2026 and the compulsory pension programme Central Provident Fund (CPF) with assets of US$513 billion, giving a total publicly known AUM of approximately US$1.97 trillion.
